Marco P: re: chaos run — tenant w/ EU residency briefly accepted writes in us-east when node fell over. Control plane still had eu as owner.
Yuki H: Did the sidecar do an autonomous acquire?
Marco P: Yes. Heartbeat missed -> local acquire -> accepted 3 writes -> network healed -> control plane later evicted us-east and reassigned eu.
Anya L: That's a residency violation. We need invariants: either forbid cross-region commits or ensure explicit signed handoff + auditable consent.
Sasha R: Thoughts on token revocation? If tokens are signed but can be revoked later we still risk short-window leaks.
Yuki H: Proposal: tokens have extremely short TTL (~10s) + monotonic nonce. Dataplane caches recent nonces (small LRU). Control plane publishes revocation stamps (epoch) that dataplane fetches periodically.
Marco P: Example header we sketched:
```
X-Handoff-Token: eyJraWQiOiJl...
X-Handoff-Issuer: eu-1
X-Handoff-Expiry: 1745001245
X-Handoff-Nonce: 0000000009
X-Handoff-Scope: cross-region
```
Anya L: For EU->US moves require witness consent: dataplane calls control-plane /witness/tenant/{id}?nonce=... and control plane replies with accept/reject + last-seen-nonce.
Sasha R: What about shadow-accept/quarantine model? Accept locally but mark writes quarantined and hidden from global reads until control plane finalizes.
Yuki H: Shadowing reduces risk but breaks read-after-write unless we surface special headers to apps. Plus merge/update conflicts get messy.
Marco P: Ops angle: we must ensure KMS-per-region keys and rapid revoke path. Also we need an operator override flow with double-authorization and audit logging.
Anya L: Legal will ask for token claims proving EU provenance: tenant_id, issuer_region, signed_time, consent_flag, custody_id. Add them to the RFC.
Sasha R: Replay protection: combine nonce + per-tenant sequence number. Dataplane keeps highest seq committed and reject lower/equal. Small state to store.
Yuki H: Two modes: local-fast (accept token + nonce cache) vs witness-strong (call witness endpoint). Default: same-region moves use local-fast; cross-region require witness unless tenant opted-in to auto-failover.
Marco P: Also consider telemetry: every token issue/accept/reject emits event to central audit stream with trace-id for postmortem.
Anya L: Can we simulate token replay, node crash, and KMS key-rotation in our sim matrix? Need to cover: nonce cache wipe, stale token after rotate, manual revoke, operator-override.
infra-bot: created ticket T-8821: "handoff-token-revoke-quarantine-poc" and attached chaos logs.
Sasha R: Next steps:
- Anya: draft RFC w/ token schema, revocation model, consent semantics.
- Yuki: PoC witness API + small nonce/seq cache in sidecar.
- Marco: ops runbook for key rotation & operator override audit.
- Sasha: sim matrix and tests.
Yuki H: I'll start with a minimal PoC: token verify stub + witness stub + nonce cache. Target: demo in 2 weeks.
Marco P: I'll loop in legal on RFC early. If we gate cross-region auto-hand-offs behind tenant consent flag it's lower risk.
Anya L: Agreed. Add audit events and explicit consent to tenant metadata.
Sasha R: Cool. I'll track the ticket and add the sim scenarios. Thanks folks. :+1:
